description: Sync issues, with their comments, and Linear Documents from the teams and projects you choose. Private-team restrictions require Enforce ACL and a successful permission read.
opening: Sync issues from the Linear teams or projects you select, and Linear Documents attached to teams, projects, issues and initiatives. Each issue is one document with its description and up to 50 of its comments. Each Linear Document is one page. A sub-issue links to its parent, and an issue links to the GitHub pull requests attached to it.

Private-team membership restricts search only when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can read the team's members. Projects and Workspace Documents carry no Linear permissions. Issue labels are not synced. Issues and documents deleted in Linear stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Access follows the team. A public team's issues can be read by everyone who can query the collection. A private team's issues can be read by its active members. A restricted team uses the members of the private team that contains it. A team's Documents resource follows the same rule. A project resource and Workspace Documents carry no Linear permissions, so set an access rule on them to restrict them.
permissions.identity: A member's email address, in lower case. Linear bots, apps and deactivated members are left out.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a team's full membership, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: Public-team access includes everyone who can query the collection, including people Linear treats as guests.

An issue in both a selected team and a selected project is stored once, and the resource that synced it last decides its access. A project gives no team audience, so set an access rule on any project you select.
Documents attached only to an initiative sit under Workspace Documents. A project document can also land there when its project belongs to more teams than HydraDB reads.

connect.auth: Linear uses a personal API key.

permissions.name: read
permissions.text: lists teams and projects, and reads issues, comments and attachments.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.text: In Linear, open Settings, Account, Security and access, API keys, and create a key.

steps.title: Select teams, projects and documents
steps.text: HydraDB lists every team, every project, a `<team> Documents` resource for each team, and one `Workspace Documents` resource. Select the ones to sync. A team's Documents resource holds the documents of the team, of its projects and of its issues. A document reachable through several teams is synced under one of them only. Workspace Documents holds documents no team claims, in practice documents attached only to an initiative.

connect.account: One connector reads what one API key's Linear user can see.

sync.first_sync: A newly selected resource reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default, measured on when items were last updated.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the issues and documents updated since the last sync.
sync.edits: An edited issue or document is picked up through its last-updated time and updates its document. Comments are read again only when their issue is picked up.
sync.deletes: Deleted issues and documents are not removed. An item that disappears from Linear stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Issues
documents.one_document: One Linear issue, with up to 50 of its comments inside it. A search result is the issue, not an individual comment.
documents.title: The issue title.
documents.text: The issue's fields, written as `name: value` lines: the description, workflow state, priority and its label, assignee and creator with their emails, creation and update times, team key and name, project name, and the issue's address. Up to 50 comments are searchable with the issue. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the issue was last updated.
documents.files: Files uploaded into the description or comments are downloaded with the connector's key and read, and their text is searchable with the issue. Only files stored by Linear's upload service are read. Link attachments, such as GitHub, Figma or plain links, are kept as references and not opened. Up to 50 link attachments are kept per issue.

attributes.name: Issue identifier
attributes.text: The identifier, such as `ENG-123`, or the issue's id when there is none. It keeps later syncs on the same document.

attributes.name: Comments
attributes.text: Up to 50 comments, each with its author, text and time, searchable with the issue. Each comment's author is recorded as a commenter.

attributes.name: Uploaded files
attributes.text: The text read from each uploaded file, searchable with the issue.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: The workflow state name, written as a line.

attributes.name: priority, priority_label
attributes.text: The priority number and its readable label, written as lines.

attributes.name: assignee, assignee_email
attributes.text: The assignee's name, or email when there is no name, and their email, written as lines. The graph records that person as the assignee.

attributes.name: reporter, reporter_email
attributes.text: The creator's name, or email when there is no name, and their email, written as lines. The graph records that person as the creator.

attributes.name: team_key, team_name
attributes.text: The owning team's key and name, written as lines.

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.text: The issue's project, if any, written as a line.

attributes.name: url
attributes.text: The issue's Linear address. It is the link back, and it is also written as a `url` line.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the issue was created, written as a line.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the issue was last updated, written as a line. Sets the result date and decides when a sync picks the issue up.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.linear_identifier
attributes.text: The identifier, such as `ENG-123`. Picks out one issue. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.linear_issue_id
attributes.text: The issue's Linear id. Picks out one issue by id. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `linear`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Team or project
attributes.text: The selected team or project the issue was synced under. A private or restricted team's members decide who can read the issue. A project carries no Linear permissions. Not searchable.

documents.name: Documents
documents.one_document: One Linear Document, attached to a team, project, issue or initiative.
documents.title: The document title.
documents.text: The document's markdown content. The author and the update time are written with it. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the document was last updated.
documents.files: Files uploaded into the content are downloaded and read, and their text is searchable with the document.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The creator's name, or email when there is no name. The graph records the document as written by that person.

attributes.name: author_email
attributes.text: The creator's email. Identifies the author in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Uploaded files
attributes.text: The text read from each uploaded file, searchable with the document.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the document was last updated, written as the `Updated` line. Sets the result date and decides when a sync picks the document up.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `linear`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Documents resource
attributes.text: The team's Documents resource the document was synced under. A private or restricted team's members decide who can read it. Workspace Documents carries no Linear permissions. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the document was created.

attributes.name: parent_type
attributes.text: What the document is attached to: `project`, `team`, `initiative` or `issue`.

attributes.name: parent_name
attributes.text: The name or identifier of what the document is attached to.

example_searches: What issues are assigned to Dana in the Platform team?
What did the comments on ENG-412 conclude?
What does our Linear project doc say about the Q4 roadmap?

connections: A sub-issue to its parent issue.

An issue to each GitHub pull request attached to it, up to 50. The link reaches the pull request when the GitHub connector also syncs that repository. A repository name capitalized differently from GitHub's does not match.
A document is not linked to the team, project, issue or initiative it is attached to.
Teams and projects appear only as text on issues, not as links.
people: The assignee and the creator of each issue.
The author of each embedded comment, as a commenter.
graph.from_text: Issue descriptions, embedded comments and document content.

not_synced: Teams, projects and Documents resources you did not select.
Comments beyond the first 50 on an issue.
Projects, cycles, milestones, labels and initiatives as items of their own.
The contents of link attachments such as GitHub, Figma and plain links. Only uploaded files are read.
Deletions: deleted issues and documents stay in HydraDB.
